Changing EXCEPT ALL to distinct EXCEPT should avoid the multiplicity bug because LeftAnti join is correct for distinct set difference.

mechanism: DataFusion's LogicalPlanBuilder::intersect_or_except lowers EXCEPT ALL to a LeftAnti HashJoinExec, so every duplicate left row matching any right row is removed rather than subtracting one occurrence per right row.

predictions.why: With multiple identical left rows and multiple identical right rows, EXCEPT ALL should subtract only the right multiplicity, but the LeftAnti join removes all matching left duplicates.
Removing the duplicate left row leaves at most one left occurrence per key, so the LeftAnti join cannot over-delete and matches EXCEPT ALL semantics.
The same lowering uses LeftSemi for INTERSECT ALL, so duplicate left rows against one matching right row should yield one row but the semi join returns all left duplicates.
UNION ALL does not use an anti or semi join for multiplicity, so duplicate left rows are preserved as expected.

mechanism: INTERSECT ALL is lowered by intersect_or_except to a LeftSemi HashJoinExec, which preserves every duplicate row from the left input that has any match on the right instead of returning the multiset minimum multiplicity.

predictions.why: Removing the left duplicate makes LeftSemi and correct INTERSECT ALL agree on one row, so this isolates the bug to duplicated left input.
If the left side has three identical rows and the right side only one, LeftSemi should still preserve all three left copies and over-return relative to the correct one-row INTERSECT ALL result.
Duplicates only on the right with a single left row should return one row under both LeftSemi and correct INTERSECT ALL, showing the failure is not caused by right duplicates alone.
When the left multiplicity exceeds the right multiplicity, LeftSemi still emits every matching left row, so the over-return should persist even though both sides contain duplicates.
